label: Measured feasibility run

dataset.name: PhysioNet / Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2017 (training set)
dataset.licence: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0
dataset.credit: Clifford GD, Liu C, Moody B, Li-wei HL, Silva I, Li Q, Johnson AE, Mark RG. AF classification from a short single lead ECG recording: The PhysioNet/computing in cardiology challenge 2017. In 2017 Computing in Cardiology (CinC) 2017 Sep 24 (pp. 1-4). IEEE.

split: Normal-rhythm and AF recordings only (5,788). Split by recording, stratified by class: 70% train, 15% validation, 15% test, so no recording is in two sets. 800 test recordings had at least one 25-beat window; 96 of them are AF.
basis: Each point in the cloud is a VALIDATION score from the search (window level, plus F1 per recording). The chosen design's headline scores are TEST results of the compiled circuit, on recordings never used for training or selection.

path.text: 256 candidate designs trained together as one batched GPU program: about 1,625 a minute, against about 28 one at a time (measured).
path.source: spike/README.md lines 45-58; spike/work/timing.json (MPS, K=256 and one-at-a-time)

path.text: The best on validation F1 (L24, 4-bit, H32, ternary) was too large: synthesis was still running at 11 minutes, past the 10-minute limit, and was stopped.
Size capped at H x L <= 128 (119 of 256 designs); best under the cap: L8, 6-bit, H16, beat-interval differences, ternary.
Checked bit for bit: 3,880 of 3,880 test windows identical to the integer model.
Per recording on the test set: sensitivity 83.3% (fails a 90% target), specificity 87.6% (passes 85%). The full-precision model scores 96.9% / 95.3%: the gap is the model, not the hardware.

size_estimate.rule: Estimated gates = k x H x (L x bits + 4): H units, each adding L inputs of 'bits' bits, then H 4-bit hidden values summed into one score. k = 2330 / 832 = 2.800.
size_estimate.calibration: Fitted to the one synthesised design (L8, 6-bit, H16: 2,330 gates after abc, spike/work/stat_gates.txt).
size_estimate.error: Reproduces the calibration design exactly by construction; there is only one measured gate count, so the general error is unknown. One check: for the L24, 4-bit, H32 design the rule gives 8,962; the spike reports 8,503 cells before gate mapping (+5.4%), and never finished mapping it. The rule ignores zero weights (ternary designs drop them) and the drr/rr difference.

notes: One seed, 60 epochs, no tuning beyond the 256 random configurations (README lines 115-118).
Configurations were drawn at random with replacement, so some repeat; each repeat was trained separately and has its own score. Ids end in the candidate's index k.
val_scores.json was written by the capped selection run (README line 69). Its best overall design, k 235, has the same validation F1 (0.7504) as the unconstrained run reported (README line 72).
The search file holds per-window sensitivity, specificity and F1, and F1 per recording; it has no per-recording sensitivity or specificity for the candidates.
Best overall and the chosen design use the source's rule: highest validation window F1, ties to fewer weights (batched.py line 162); the chosen one only among H x L <= 128.
Only the chosen design's weights were saved (work/best.json), plus the failed large design (work/best_large.json); gate counts for other candidates would need retraining.
The 90% sensitivity and 85% specificity targets are the dashboard's example targets, not part of the spike.
Gate count and depth are Yosys cell count and longest topological path, not a real cell library's area or timing (README line 122).
The bit-for-bit check uses the spike's own netlist evaluator, not a second simulator (README lines 100-101).
All numbers are from one feasibility spike written during the event, 21 Nov 2026.
